title: Runtime handshake and streaming/tool-call conformance for onboarded models
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Create an automated conformance and verification suite that validates streaming I/O and function/tool-calling semantics for every newly onboarded model variant and for pinned model versions. This ticket covers the runtime handshake tests, message framing, streaming incremental delta semantics, tool/function calling initiation and resolution, and the end-to-end integration with published performance profiles (latency/throughput). The goal is to ensure that when we publish a model with a performance profile and a pinned runtime version, the model behaves correctly under streaming + tool call workloads and that the published profile is representative of expected median and tail latency.

Out of scope: exhaustive fuzzing of model outputs, non-deterministic model behavior unrelated to streaming semantics, and performance microbenchmarks not tied to conformance thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Automated suite runs as part of onboarding pipeline and returns pass/fail for streaming semantics
All supported tool/function call patterns (sync call, async notify, streaming result pipes) are exercised and validated against the runtime contract
If a pinned model version fails conformance, publishing of its performance profile is blocked and the onboarding job flags the model for manual review
Observed latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for streaming+tool-call benchmarks are within 20% of the published profile for the selected test workload
Conformance reports are stored in S3 and linked on the model catalog entry; failures create bug issues with reproduction harness attached
checklist: Design handshake test vectors (initial draft) - Aisha
Implement runtime-level framing checks and KV cache reuse assertions - Marco
Add tool-call scenarios (function return, tool streaming via chunked attachments, cancellations) - Marco
Integrate perf measurements into conformance run and compare against profile - Bench team
Hook test into onboarding CI pipeline; block profile publish on failure - CI
Add human-readable conformance summary to model catalog UI - Console team
test_plan: 1) Synthetic harness that drives the runtime with deterministic seed prompts and mock tool endpoints. 2) For each model variant (float32, q8, q4), run the following matrix: cold-start stream, warm-stream with reused KV, tool-invocation where tool streams content back, tool cancellation mid-stream. 3) Capture event traces, frame IDs, and model tokens; assert ordering, no duplicate frames, and correct EOS signals. 4) Measure p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput for the exact workload used in the model's perf profile. 5) Run negative tests with malformed frames and ensure graceful runtime error and no state corruption.
results_summary:
Initial alpha runs against three recently onboarded models:
- variant-a (float32): passed all semantic checks; p95 within 12% of published profile.
- variant-b (q8): streaming order violation observed in 2/200 runs when mid-stream tool cancellation occurred; root cause likely kernel-level token flush race.
- variant-c (q4): passed semantics but p99 is 28% worse than profile for the long-stream workload; likely due to slower decode path under quantization.

Next actions: create targeted reproducer for variant-b, add gating rule to block profile publish on p99 > 25% delta, and engage runtime team to investigate kernel scheduling for q4 path.
